text:
Sam: Heads-up — submitting a formal ask for additional GPU capacity in EU next quarter. Need to sync on numbers + billing artifacts before I put this in the finance queue. :eyes:
Maria: Outline please — how many GPUs, which region, why not burst/spot?
Sam: Proposal summary: add 8 H100s to eu-central-1 for inference (low-latency region for EU customers). Current issue: tail latency on large request profiles is spiking during business hours and model quality degrades if we fallback to smaller variants.
Sam: Cost delta estimates (rough):
```
- Pay-as-you-go: ~ $28.8k / month (~$345k / year)
- 12mo commitment (discount expected): ~ $20.2k / month (~$242k / year) => ~30% savings
- 36mo commitment: ~ $17.3k / month (~$208k / year) => ~40% savings
```
Maria: Link to the cost workbook and perf slides: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1GpuBudgetExample (see tab "eu-h100-ask") :thumbsup:
billing-bot: FYI — latest invoices show a one-off egress spike on invoice INV-2026-03-14 for $12,450 (us-west-2). Flagged and assigned to @Maria for investigation.
Maria: Confirmed, I started a billing ticket with cloud provider. Early hypothesis: large snapshot sync from a test pool accidentally triggered cross-region transfer. Requesting credit.
Elaine: Before we approve a multi-year commitment we need SLA/ROI and locking risks spelled out. Can you add: expected p95 latency improvement, estimated avoidance of model fallbacks, and steady-state utilization assumptions?
Ravi: Quick perf note — switching these locs to H100 reduces average token time by ~20% on our benchmark and cuts p95 by ~180-220ms. On traffic mix we observed a 12% reduction in calls routed to smaller models (so less cost on fallback).
Taylor: FP&A questions: what's the approval ask? Capex vs opex? If we go 12mo reserve is this charged as committed spend (operational) or prepay? We need the exact invoice schedule. Also need a comparison to buying Dedicated capacity via Redwood Dedicated offers (any internal offsets?).
Sam: Ask: approve line-item of $250k/year (conservative) to cover a 12mo reservation + buffer and to allow burst headroom. We can break into quarterly approvals if that helps. If finance prefers, we can do payg for first month while negotiations/credits wrap up.
Maria: Added amortization scenarios to sheet (tab "finance-frames"). Also attached the billing export CSV for the last 3 months in that tab.
Sam: Small calc snippet I used to build numbers:```bash
H100_hour=5.0  # assumed
GPUs=8
month_hours=720
monthly_payg=$(echo "$H100_hour * $GPUs * $month_hours" | bc)
```
Sam: That gives the ballpark above — exact vendor quotes pending.
Elaine: Ok schedule a 15-min review with FP&A and infra leadership. Add ROI bullets + risk table to the sheet and @Taylor I'll need your signoff on the amortization approach.
Taylor: I'll review the sheet this afternoon. If we can reduce the ask to $200k/yr with a clear 6-9 month payback, easier to route.
Maria: Billing ticket update: provider acknowledged the egress; they opened a credit case (Case 99012). If that comes through it's ~ $12.4k back to ops which lowers the near-term hit.
Ravi: One more thought — we should also consider a smaller initial commit (4 H100) + dynamic burst to 8 using spot for non-SLA traffic. That reduces committed spend but preserves perf for critical routes.
Sam: Good option. I'll add a 4+burst scenario in the sheet and include sensitivity to token-volume growth + caching gains from Redwood Optimize.
Sam: Can @Elaine or @Taylor mark earliest available times for the 15-min? Planning to push to finance by EOD Wed if we have leadership OK. :raise_hand:
